title: Grips within pair terms on the field of identical objects, and their weighing

key_results.statement: For every real $F$ on $\{0,\dots,N_f\}$, $G_F=\sum_k\Delta^kF(0)\sum_x\lvert x\rangle\langle x\rvert\otimes S\otimes e_k(P^{(1)}_x,\dots,P^{(N_f)}_x)$, the $k$-th term acting on the body and $k$ field objects together; exact.

For $N_f\ge2$, $G_F$ is a sum of pair terms (on $\mathcal H$, or on $\mathcal H_{\rm adm}$ when the body is the only object of its type) iff $\Delta^kF(0)=0$ for $2\le k\le N_f$, iff $F(\Phi)=\alpha+\beta\Phi$; adding or moving listed pair terms does not change this; exact characterization, no control in the class; $F=\Phi^2$ (a three-object term) is an illustration outside the class.

For $N_f=1$ every $F$ is the affine grip $\alpha=F(0)$, $\beta=F(1)-F(0)$; for every $N_f\ge1$ the grips within pair terms are the affine grips, each the full grip $\beta\Phi$ plus the own term $\alpha S$, and different $(\alpha,\beta)$ give different $C$.

Affine grip, held body, stated state: $E_{k,\sigma}=\alpha\sigma M_k+c_s+N_f\varepsilon_0(x)$, $\mathrm{Cost}_{k,\sigma}=\alpha\sigma M_k+C^{\rm mark}_{k,\sigma}$, with $C^{\rm mark}$ that of the full grip at $g_b=\sigma\beta M_k$; exact.

$\mathrm{Cost}^{(1)}=\sigma M_k(\alpha+\beta n)$, $\Delta W^{(1)}=\mu\Omega\,\mathrm{Cost}^{(1)}$ at first order in $g_s$, mark fraction $\mu=\beta n/(\alpha+\beta n)$ independent of level and branch, self-cost $C^{\rm self}=-ng_b\chi_s[1+O(\chi)]$, $C^{\rm self}<0$ exactly for $\beta\ne0$; excluded $g_s=0$, $\beta=0$, $\alpha+\beta n=0$, $[\ell]=0$; for $\chi\ll1$ the cost vanishes only where $\mu\chi_s=1+O(\chi)$ and a level gap only where $\lvert\mu\rvert\chi\ge\frac12-O(\chi)$, both excluded by $\lvert\mu\rvert\chi\ll1$.

For every affine grip with $\beta\ne0$, $\alpha+\beta n\ne0$, every level and both branches, first order in $g_s$, $\chi\ll1$, cancellations (c1)–(c4) excluded: $\Delta W=\Omega(1+B^{\rm fg})[\mu\,\mathrm{Cost}^{(1)}+C^{\rm self}]$, a rewriting of (3.14) of 07-ilang-weight/03-weight-of-mark; at fixed $\beta$, $\Delta W$ does not depend on $\alpha$ (the rest term is not weighed); holds for every affine grip, no control in the class.

Under the conditions of (3.6), $\lvert\mu\rvert\chi\ll1$ and $\chi q\ll1$, on the three graphs: $\Delta W=\mathrm{Cost}\,\mu\Omega[1+B^F]$, mark weighing ratio $w=1+B^F$, $B^F=-\frac{g_b}{2t_f}[\ell(r)+\ell(r')+2(1-\mu)\ell_0-T_2]+O(\chi^2q)+O(\epsilon^2)$ with absolute constants (3.16), $T_2$ exact, $\epsilon=(1+\lvert\mu\rvert)\chi+\lvert B^{\rm fg}\rvert$.

Under the conditions of (3.6), $[\ell]\ne0$ and $\chi q\ll1$, $q=1+\lvert T_2\rvert/\ell_0+\bar T_3/\ell_0^2$, $\bar T_3=2s_3/(\mathcal X^2\lvert[\ell]\rvert)\ge\lvert T_3\rvert$: the self-cost carries the weight $\Delta W-\Delta W^{(1)}$, and its weighing ratio against the first-order part is $w^{\rm self}=\mu^{-1}[1+\zeta+O(\chi q)]$ with an absolute constant (3.16), so its error is $O(\chi q/\lvert\mu\rvert)$; $\zeta=(\ell(r)+\ell(r')-T_2)/(2\ell_0)$, $T_2$ exact, the same for every affine grip, level and branch; $B^F=(w^{\rm self}-1)C^{\rm self}/\mathrm{Cost}$ exactly.

Non-degeneracy: a pair is $c$-non-degenerate ($c>0$ fixed as $L$ grows) if $\lvert[\ell]\rvert\ge c$ (square torus), $\ge c\,m/L^2$ (cubic torus) or $\ge c\,m$ (ring), $m=\max(\lvert r\rvert,\lvert r'\rvert)$; there $\lvert T_2\rvert\le2C/c$, $\bar T_3\le4C/c$ (square), $\lvert T_2\rvert\le4C/(cL)$, $\bar T_3\le4C/(cL^2)$ (cubic), $\bar T_3\le2CL^2/c$ (ring), and on the ring $T_2/\ell_0\le2$ at every pair with $[\ell]\ne0$; so $q=O(1)$ at these pairs of the three graphs; a sufficient condition, holding for $1\ll\lvert r\rvert,\lvert r'\rvert\ll L$ when the distances differ by a fixed factor.

Ring, exact for $[\ell]\ne0$: $\zeta=1-\frac{2+4(\varrho+\varrho')}{L^2-1}$, $\varrho=\lvert r\rvert(L-\lvert r\rvert)$; at $c$-non-degenerate pairs (3.15): square torus $\zeta=1-\frac{\ln(\lvert r\rvert\lvert r'\rvert)+O(1)}{4\pi\ell_0}$, cubic torus $\zeta=\frac{1}{8\pi\ell_0}(\lvert r\rvert^{-1}+\lvert r'\rvert^{-1})+O(\lvert r\rvert^{-3}+\lvert r'\rvert^{-3}+L^{-1})$; so there $\zeta\to0$ on the cubic torus at large distance and $\zeta\ll1$ on the square torus only where $\ln\frac{L^2}{\lvert r\rvert\lvert r'\rvert}\ll\ln L$; at other torus pairs $\zeta$ carries $-T_2/(2\ell_0)$ with $T_2$ exact; on the ring $\zeta\ne0$ at every pair, $\zeta\to1$ for $\lvert r\rvert,\lvert r'\rvert\ll L$.

On every graph of the class, at every pair with $[\ell]\ne0$, first order in $g_s$, exactly: $1+B^{\rm fg}=\frac{[\ell_e]}{[\ell]}\frac{1-\frac\eta2(\ell_e(r)+\ell_e(r'))}{1+\eta^2\ell'_e/\mathcal X}$ and $\mu w^{\rm self}=1-\frac{1-\eta\ell_e(0)}{\eta\ell_e(0)}B^{\rm fg}$; for $\chi\le\frac14$, $\chi q\le1$: $B^{\rm fg}=-\eta\ell_0\zeta+O(\chi^2q)$ and $\mu w^{\rm self}=1+\zeta+O(\chi q)$ with absolute constants, their derivatives in $g_b$ likewise; so the remainders of (3.5), (3.7)–(3.9), (3.13) are uniform in $D$, $L$ and the places.

Under the conditions of (3.13), with $0<\mu_-\le1$, $\mu_+\ge2$ fixed: (i) for $\mu_-\le\lvert\mu\rvert\le\mu_+$, $w^{\rm self}=1+O(\chi q)$ iff $\mu=1+\zeta+O(\chi q)$, i.e. $\alpha=0$ where $\zeta\to0$ and $\alpha=-\beta n/2$ where $\zeta\to1$; (ii) for $\alpha=0$, $w^{\rm self}=1+\zeta+O(\chi q)$ and $\Delta W=\mathrm{Cost}\,\Omega[1-\eta\ell_0\zeta+O(\chi^2q)]$, like the first-order part on the cubic torus at $c$-non-degenerate pairs up to $O(1/\min(\lvert r\rvert,\lvert r'\rvert))$, on the square torus at such pairs only where $\ln\frac{L^2}{\lvert r\rvert\lvert r'\rvert}\ll\ln L$, on the ring only near $4(\varrho+\varrho')=L^2$; small $\mu$: $w^{\rm self}=(1+\zeta+O(\chi q))/\mu$ grows as $(1+\zeta)/\mu$ and is not fixed at this order for $\lvert\mu\rvert\lesssim\chi q$ (control: ring $L=4$, $\zeta=-1$, $\mu=\chi_s$ gives $w^{\rm self}=26/25+O(\chi)$); two bodies share $\mu\Omega$ iff $\alpha_1\beta_2=\alpha_2\beta_1$.

Two internal states of one body with an affine grip, first order in $g_s$, $\chi\ll1$, $\lvert\mu\rvert\chi\ll1$, $\chi q\ll1$, (c1)–(c4) excluded: $\Delta W_a-\Delta W_{a'}=(\mathrm{Cost}_a-\mathrm{Cost}_{a'})\mu\Omega[1-\frac{g_a+g_{a'}}{2t_f}(\ell(r)+\ell(r')+2(1-\mu)\ell_0-T_2)+O((1+\lvert\mu\rvert)^2\chi^2q)]$ with an absolute constant (3.16), i.e. $\mathcal F_i=\mu_i\phi$.

open_issues: The size of O(ηK) of (4.10) on each graph is that of 07-ilang-weight/04-weight-of-bond; the constants C of (3.15), the O(1) terms of (3.14) on the two tori and the absolute constant K of (3.16) are not evaluated.

At pairs that are not c-non-degenerate, in particular on the ring at two places at nearly equal distance from the source, T̄_3 and hence q may grow with L (on the ring T_2/ℓ_0 ≤ 2 and the signed T_3 = O(ℓ_0²) stay bounded); the remainders there are bounded through q by (3.16), and sharper bounds would need the signed quotients [ℓ^(k)]/[ℓ] of all orders.
For |μ| ≲ χq the weight of the self-cost is given only on a fixed graph, at the next order (ν_1), with a remainder whose constant depends on the graph and the pair.
(3.15) is a sufficient condition; at pairs where it fails, ζ and the criteria (3.8), (3.11) are stated with T_2 exact and are not reduced to distances.
The bond criterion uses the midpoint as the place of the pair; with body 1 as the place its first breaking term is κ of (4.10), on the ring ρ_0^ring − 1 of (4.12).
Grips outside pair terms (N_f ≥ 2, F not affine) are not admissible descriptions under A5; only the illustration (3.12) is computed for them.
On the admissible subspace, (3.2) assumes the body is the only object of its type; several identical bodies are treated only through the identity on the full space.
Grips with a different internal operator for each value of Φ_x, field states other than the stated one, and fields of cells are outside the scope.

consistency_checks.check: Special grips: α=0 reproduces the full-grip results (3.14) of 07-ilang-weight/03-weight-of-mark and (4.9), (4.10) of 07-ilang-weight/04-weight-of-bond; α=1, β=γ reproduces F^(a) and B^(a) of (3.15) of 07-ilang-weight/03-weight-of-mark exactly, (4.9) for coupling (a), and (4.13)
Dimensions: α, β, μ, Ω, χ, ζ, T_2, B^F, w^self, ρ^F are numbers; g_b, Cost, C^self, ΔW and the bond cost are costs
